title: Static TEST-gate check still false-passes on a same-line comment containing "TEST &&" or "TEST ?" — FIND-605's tightening reduced but did not eliminate the grep weakness
description: The seam-gating loop now does grep -vE "TEST (&&|\?)" (test-record-earn.sh:18), an improvement over the bare "TEST" of sprint-6. But it still operates on raw text: a future edit that reads an env UNGUARDED yet shares a line with a comment containing the literal 'TEST &&' or 'TEST ?' (e.g. `const x = process.env.HOME; // restore TEST && prod behavior`) would be removed by grep -v and FALSE-PASS the gate. The check is textual, not syntactic — it cannot distinguish a real `TEST &&` guard from the same characters in a comment/string on the matching line. The behavioral prod-mode backstop (test 12, test-record-earn.sh:82-86) only covers HOME, not the other 8 seams, so for FOUNDER_RAW_LOGS_JSON et al. the static grep is the SOLE prod-ignore guarantee. Not an active fabrication path in current code (all seams are genuinely TEST-gated), but the guard against a future un-gated seam is bypassable.

evidence.snippet:
for seam in FOUNDER_DIR ... FOUNDER_RAW_LOGS_JSON BASE_RPC_URL HOME; do
  bad="$(grep -n "process\.env\.$seam" <<<"$src" | grep -vE "TEST (&&|\?)" || true)"
  ok "$([ -z "$bad" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "STATIC: $seam read is TEST-gated (${bad:-none})"
done

fix: Replace (or backstop) the static grep with a per-seam BEHAVIORAL prod-mode assertion like test 12: for EACH seam, run with FOUNDER_TEST unset and the seam set to a poison value, and assert it is ignored (root/wallet/cursor/logs unaffected, no fabricated row). That tests the actual runtime gate and cannot be fooled by comments. At minimum, strip comments before the grep (e.g. sed 's://.*::') so a commented 'TEST &&' cannot mask an un-gated read.
